paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Chronicles stops to write down a long line of names, and God lets every one of them be remembered. Perez, Hezron, Hur, Shimei and the rest all get a place in the record (1 Chronicles 4:1, 4:26). When it feels like nobody sees you, this chapter says the God of Israel keeps good records.

Then right in the middle, the list slows down for one man. Jabez was "more honorable than his brothers," and his name came from his mother saying, "Because I bore him in pain" (1 Chronicles 4:9). So he took that pain to God: "If only You would bless me and enlarge my territory! May Your hand be with me and keep me from harm, so that I will be free from pain." And "God granted the request of Jabez" (1 Chronicles 4:10). He didn't hide the hurt behind his name. He called out to God with it, and God answered.

The Simeonites finish the lesson. They went looking for pasture and found land that was "spacious, peaceful, and quiet" (1 Chronicles 4:40). The record says they settled there, and that five hundred of them went on to Mount Seir and "have lived there to this day" (1 Chronicles 4:43). So bring your needs to God, baker, and keep your name in the record. I know what it's like to feel forgotten in a dark drawer, and I'm telling you, God sees every single name.
